content.content:
#### Details

An open task takes the tab's place, with a back arrow and the task's mode and name along its top, the arrow and <Escape> going back to the list as it was left. Opening a task that has run or is running also opens it in a tab of its own in the body, as a file opens, as the [BodyScope](../../../../scope/application/Body.md#body-scope) says, showing its header and output there, unless it is a task the Chat tab shows, one running or the one it shows while none runs, when Chat is selected instead, with that task selected in its header. What the open task shows, top to bottom:
- Status: its status label and how long it took, or has been running, as the MessageList writes them, on one line
- Prompt: its prompt, as it was typed, in a GrowingTextInputScope, and beneath it what is attached to it
- Steps: for a chain, its steps, as its chain steps say, with Add step; a task that isn't a chain has no Steps section
- Details: the rest at a glance, its lane, its place in the queue while it waits, the conversation it carries on or that it starts a new one, its model and effort, and once it has run, how many tool calls it made, its errors, its tokens and their cost, and how many files it changed, each a labelled figure, those that don't apply left out
- Parameters: its mode, its model and effort, its Slice toggle, and whether it starts a new conversation, each as the chat input shows it
- Actions: Resend, Send to Spec or Send to Code, Cancel while it is under way or queued, and Open output, as the PromptSendingScope gives them
A long prompt is clipped: past 8 lines, as they wrap at the tab's width, the Prompt section shows its first 8 and fades the last of them into the section's background, with a "Read more" link beneath, in the theme's accent, with a down chevron. Clicking it shows the whole prompt, the link reading "Show less" with an up chevron, which clips it again, scrolling the tab back to the Prompt section if it had scrolled past it. A prompt of 8 lines or fewer shows whole, with no link. It starts clipped each time a task is opened. Clicking into a queued task's prompt to edit it shows it whole, as it is being typed in, and it is clipped again once the task is opened afresh. Clipping only changes what shows: its attachments are listed beneath either way, and copying or editing takes the whole prompt.
A queued task is edited right there: its prompt can be typed in, its attachments removed, and its parameters changed, its mode among those of the tabs, a change of lane moving it to that lane's queue in its place. Each change is saved with the project as it is made, as saving a queued prompt's edit is, and while it is being changed the task is held, never sent, as a queued prompt being edited is; going back, or opening another, lets it go. A task that has run, or is running, can't be changed: its prompt and parameters read as they were sent, and "Edit and resend" puts them in the open task as a new queued prompt, ready to change, sent once "Send" is clicked. The chat input's own <Up> editing still works as the [ChatInputScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, and opens the same task here.

#### Chain Steps
#### Chain Steps

An open Chain task lists its steps in its Steps section, beneath its prompt and above its details, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the ste
